Lemma
[Continuity of integration against the parametrix] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0259, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0260 ↗ def:chow-iii-ch23-parametrix 1. ch23:23.25\group Convolution differentiation

If $f:\mathcal M\times [0,T]\to \mathbb R$ is continuous, then \[ I_N(x,t,u)=\int P_N(x,z,t-u)f(z,u)\, d\mu (z) \] is continuous, converges uniformly to $f(x,u)$ as $t\searrow u$, and is smooth in $(x,t)$ with derivatives obtained by differentiating under the integral.
Proof

\sketch Split the integral into a small normal ball and its complement. The Gaussian bound makes the complement exponentially small and the normal-coordinate change of variables reduces the ball to the Euclidean approximate identity; dominated convergence handles all derivatives.

□
